decision: Needs-correction; final G3 pending actual evidence

findings.title: Limit duplicate-username mapping to its own INSERT constraint
findings.trigger: A role/membership/audit/pending-session necessary write returns SQLSTATE 23505 for a different uniqueness failure.
findings.observed: The whole transaction's DbError is mapped solely by SQLSTATE 23505 to HTTP 409 with a username-already-exists message.
findings.impact: The real necessary-write failure is mislabeled as an existing username, so clients receive the wrong recoverability and reason despite rollback. Username uniqueness is only one constraint within the transaction.
findings.requiredCorrection: Before DbError erases SQLx constraint metadata, recognize only platform_user INSERT with SQLSTATE 23505 and constraint platform_user_username_unique as explicit username-conflict outcome. Leave all other SQL errors as Database and roll back normally; no shared DbError or other-command expansion is needed.
findings.requiredActualVerification: Same-username contention still has one success and one 409. Inject non-username 23505 at necessary association/audit/session writes, require 500 and exact whole-transaction rollback plus successful clean retry.

staticAlignmentObservations: Typed UUID parsing and HashSet reject aliases of the same role before any write; audit role IDs are normalized actual identities.
Existing role IDs are locked in UUID order FOR SHARE, followed by primary organization FOR SHARE; active/not-found checks use those rows within the create transaction.
The database-generated user UUID and row version are materialized before real active role and primary-membership rows are inserted.
Response serialization, required creation audit and pending-session CAS flush all occur before the same transaction commit; rejected outcomes explicitly roll back.

The historical W01 test was renamed and updated to current relationship success/404/409 semantics, remaining explicitly ignored behind its controlled R2D harness. It is not actual validation of the new batch.
Only the scoped create path and its store helpers/test changed; other user commands retain their existing boundaries.
